Gemini Robotics 2.5 pilots Apollo 2 parts kitting at Mercedes-Benz

Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5 on November 10, reporting an Apptronik Apollo 2 pilot on Mercedes-Benz lines in Kecskemét and Sindelfingen. It reports 96% success picking metal brackets from bulk bins into sequencing trays.

Humanoids Daily ↗10 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 2

A release with factory-pilot results

Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5 on November 10, reporting an Apptronik Apollo 2 pilot on Mercedes-Benz lines in Kecskemét and Sindelfingen. It reports 96% success picking metal brackets from bulk bins into sequencing trays.

Reasoning and movement

Gemini Robotics ER tracks the workflow while 2.5 controls hands and arms, including corrections after imperfect grasps or placements. DeepMind reports evaluation on over 200 tasks, with success increasing 30–100% depending on task type and completion 20–30% faster than previous baselines. These are company evaluations.

Proof of concept and partner access

The factory work is a proof of concept, not evidence of full deployment across production lines. The announcement does not provide the trial count behind 96% or cycle time against people. Rollout is to robotics partners, without announced public API pricing. Argon assisted simulation and failure analysis during development.
